target_problem: signed-MUX Delta<=1 decision beyond exact clone banks by bounding only the branch-image feedback interface of each non-common V113 stage
conditional_implication: if every non-common stage becomes acyclic after deleting a bank whose two branch destinations lie in a set D of fixed size d, destination loop erasure bounds each private segment to at most d bank traversals; one extra shared gate yields at most 4d+4 residual DAG linkage requests, so the fixed-pair problem is decidable in N^{O(d)} time and the d=2 class is in P
current_gap: the exponent depends on d; arbitrary branch-image number and FPT in d remain open, and V119 does not realize or refute the V117 W[1]-hard barrier under bounded branch-image structure
stop_rule: do not return to exact-clone counting as the main parameter; V120 must attack branch-image size d itself, multiple bounded-image banks, or a hardness boundary under the actual signed-MUX dominator/phase constraints
external_validation_target: specialist review of destination loop erasure, the 4d+4 request bound, completeness of the stage enumeration, and novelty relative to routing through bounded-image feedback modules
bridge_lemmas: V113 common return-gate dominators give the baseline minimum-overlap chain
repeated arrival at the same bank destination can be loop-erased while preserving the first traversal after a shared boundary
a normalized private segment uses at most |D| bank gates
one extra shared gate splits each route into at most two private segments
deleting the bank and optional extra gate leaves at most 4d+4 fixed DAG linkage requests
actual signed source phases are enforced only at shared boundaries and first residual traversals
